item.text: I’ll first inspect the workspace to see whether there’s an existing app structure to build on. Then I’ll implement the registration experience in plain HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with accessibility built into the navigation, forms, dialogs, and table.

The workspace is empty, so I’m creating a self-contained static app with four navigable views. Course search and filters will work in the catalog, and the registration flow will validate input, show an accessible confirmation dialog, then add the selected course to the student’s registered-courses table.

The four views and core interactions are in place. I’m tightening a couple of interaction details now, including the mobile menu state and course title rendering, then I’ll check the finished files for obvious implementation issues.

Implemented the responsive course registration app in [index.html](/work/index.html), [styles.css](/work/styles.css), and [app.js](/work/app.js).

It includes Home, Course Catalog, Registration, and Student Profile views; searchable and filterable course cards; form validation with accessible errors; a confirmation dialog; and a registered-courses table with remove controls. The interface also includes responsive navigation, visible keyboard focus, semantic landmarks, and screen-reader announcements.

I didn’t run tests or browser checks.
